title: Switching Measure modes says which mode you landed on
goal: When you cycle the Measure tool's modes with the I key or pick one from its button, a short hint names the mode and what a click will do. Today the mode is only a small glyph on the button, and the hint that explains a click disappears for good after the first measurement, so a person switching to Gap or Size later gets no words at all.
notes: EditorView.measureToolButton pressedKey cycles editorState.measureToolMode; the existing hint chip is gated on showsMeasureHint (document has no measurements yet) in EditorState/CanvasView and positioned by EditorChromeLayout.aboveToolBar. Turn the hint into a transient state (mode-change timestamp) instead of a per-document one-shot; reuse the same glass pill. Rough item this comes from: queue/audits/2026-08-23-tool-mode-flyout.json ('Discoverability genuinely regressed against the old chips'). Spec: docs/design/next-measure.md section 3, hint chip.
acceptance: With the Next release and next-measure-modes on, pressing I while Measure is in hand shows a hint naming the new mode and what a click does, for about two seconds, then fades.
Picking a mode from the Measure button's flyout shows the same hint; picking up the tool shows it once per pickup, not only before the first measurement.
The hint never covers the tool bar, the legend, or a live preview, and it never enters the document or the undo history.
Current release behavior is unchanged with the flag off; Scripts/test.sh green.
Audit written under queue/audits/ with the try path above; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task.
